config.title: Type controlled input handlers

intro.title: Type controlled input handlers
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with a text input field that uses TypeScript to ensure type safety. You will learn how to create controlled input handlers, which manage form state by updating a variable with every keystroke. The core concept involves using TypeScript types to define the shape of your state and event handlers, preventing common runtime errors. You'll work with React's useState hook for state management and TypeScript interfaces to type your events. By the end, you'll have a typed input component that logs user input to the console in a type-safe way.
intro.usecase: Type-controlled input handlers are essential for building robust forms and interactive dashboards in real-world applications. For example, in a financial dashboard, you would use them to ensure that a user entering a stock quantity provides a valid number, preventing errors in calculations. Similarly, in a user registration form, they enforce that email fields contain properly formatted strings before submission. This pattern is also critical in admin panels with dynamic filters, where typed handlers validate search parameters like date ranges or numeric thresholds, ensuring data integrity and a smooth user experience.

objectives: Implement a typed state variable to store input values
Construct a type-safe event handler for input changes
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define input event parameter types
Bind the typed handler to an input element's onChange event
Control input behavior by manipulating the typed state value
Integrate type annotations to prevent runtime input errors
Render a form with controlled inputs using TypeScript types

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, enabling the use of React and useState in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check the syntax: import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

// Create the App component here

steps.title: Define the state interface
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a TypeScript interface named FormState with a single property 'textField' of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a FormState interface ready to type your component's state.
successCriteria: A FormState interface is defined with a textField property of type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Inside the App component, call useState with an initial value that matches FormState, providing the type parameter.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with the FormState interface as the type parameter, and provide an initial object with the required properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state initialization
const [user, setUser] = useState<User>({ name: '', age: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The useState hook is called with FormState as the type parameter and an initial object matching the interface.
successCriteria: useState is called with FormState type parameter
State variable and setter are destructured
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to provide the FormState type parameter to useState and an initial object with name and email properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState<FormState> with an initial object like { name: '', email: '' }.

steps.title: Define the input change handler
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function named handleInputChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the state.
steps.hint: The function should use the setFormState updater to modify the state based on the input's name and value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed handleInputChange function is defined inside the App component, ready to be used with input elements.
successCriteria: The handleInputChange function is defined with the correct parameter type and updates the formState using setFormState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the state using setFormState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInputChange function is not defined correctly. It should take a typed event parameter and update the formState.
